key_insight: Locus improves medical image classification by regularizing attention so the model focuses more on anatomically relevant foreground regions and less on background.
clinical_relevance: This could make classifiers more reliable and interpretable across imaging tasks by encouraging attention to align with meaningful anatomy without requiring manual segmentation labels.
method: Uses pretrained segmentation foundation models to extract anatomical shape priors.
Adds an attention regularization term that penalizes background-dominant attention rather than forcing exact pixel-level mask matching.
Applies the framework across diverse modalities and anatomical targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on eight medical imaging datasets spanning dermoscopy, X-ray, histopathology, and cardiac MRI, with consistent classification gains and more anatomically grounded attention.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and generalizability of the foundation-model-derived anatomical masks, which may vary across modalities and datasets.
paper_title: Learning To Focus: Anatomy-Guided Attention Regularization for Medical Image Classification
